title: fix(imap): cap max_command_size to prevent auth-line heap amplification
description:
Security fix. The imap-next Options::default() sets max_command_size to ~26 MiB. An attacker can send AUTHENTICATE PLAIN <26 MB base64> before any auth check, causing ~19 MiB heap allocation per connection. With 200 concurrent connections (the semaphore limit) that is ~3.8 GiB of heap allocation per attack wave.

Fix: in run_session_inner (session/mod.rs), after Options::default(), set options.max_command_size = 8 * 1024 (8 KiB). Add max_command_size_bytes: u64 to LimitsConfig in config.rs with a default of 8192, so it is operator-configurable. Update TOML deserialization and Config::validate to enforce max_command_size >= 256 (sane minimum).

Note: imap-next requires max_literal_size <= max_command_size is NOT an invariant — they are independent limits. max_literal_size governs APPEND/literal payloads; max_command_size governs the command line itself. Verify by reading Options source before writing.

Acceptance: cargo test -p stoa-imap passes; a command line exceeding 8 KiB causes CommandTooLong error, not buffering.
